City council approves new cycle lanes after year-long debate

By Priya Raman · 14 March 2026
Share on X Email

The city council voted 9–4 on Thursday night to build 22 kilometres of protected cycle lanes over the next three years, ending a debate that has divided residents since last spring.

The plan, first proposed by councillor Mark Osei, will remove about 400 parking spaces in the city centre. Shop owners on Market Street had argued that fewer spaces would mean fewer customers, while cycling groups pointed to studies from other cities showing the opposite.

What changes first

Work starts in May on Market Street and the river path. The council says each section will be finished within eight weeks, and that buses will keep their current routes.

  • Market Street: 3.2 km, opening in July
  • River path link: 1.1 km, opening in August
  • Station Road: 4.5 km, opening next spring

“This is the biggest change to how people get around the centre in forty years,” Osei said after the vote.
